behavior: Calls the production version parser with two valid release lines and three invalid forms (prerelease, leading-zero patch, unrecognized text), asserting the parsed value or None for each.
failure_caught: The parser accepting a prerelease or leading-zero version as a stable release, or dropping the `codex-cli ` prefix rule.
criticality_reason: Version parsing is diagnostic only; a wrong value is shown to the user but never gates a launch.
signal_reason: Five inputs pin the prefix, suffix and canonical-release grammar, including both rejection shapes.
uniqueness_reason: versions::tests covers the numeric parser; the codex-specific prefix/suffix rule is only asserted here.
fidelity_reason: Direct call to the production parser.
recommendation_reason: Small exact grammar test; keep.

behavior: Creates terminal sessions through `terminal create ... agent run cursor-cloud -- <account>` for a configured and an unconfigured account; asserts the created kind, the configured preview text and exact account/commit/model/exclusion lines, one bridge start total, no CreateAgent/Send/CancelRun, scratch cleanup on Enter, and an error naming the unconfigured account for the other.
failure_caught: An unknown account starting a bridge or reaching preview, the preview omitting the exact published commit/model, or the owned scratch tree surviving session close.
criticality_reason: Account selection and preview are the gate before any cloud mutation; a wrong account can act on the wrong repository, and a leaked scratch tree holds private data.
signal_reason: Both accounts are driven through the real CLI/server, the event stream is counted for starts and mutations, and process liveness plus scratch existence are checked.
uniqueness_reason: Only configured-vs-unconfigured CLI creation test; the managed preview tests start from a known account.
fidelity_reason: Real CLI, server and PTY with a scripted bridge fixture; the provider side is the controlled dependency.
recommendation_reason: Account gate and cleanup evidence; keep.

behavior: For four termination modes (Enter, SIGTERM to the session, SIGKILL of the adapter, server CloseTerminal), asserts the preview names the exact HEAD/account/repository/model/exclusion and prepare semantics, the bridge method sequence is GetVersion/Me/ListModels/ListRepositories, then that the scratch root, bridge pid and adapter pid are gone, no mutations occurred, local edits remain untouched and HEAD is unchanged.
failure_caught: An exit path leaving the owned bridge, adapter or scratch tree alive, mutating the repository or remote, or a preview that misstates the published commit.
criticality_reason: Leaked adapter/bridge processes and scratch trees persist private prompt data; a preview naming the wrong commit misleads the user about what will be sent.
signal_reason: Four independent termination paths each assert process death and scratch removal, with local-edit and HEAD preservation and a no-mutation event scan.
uniqueness_reason: Only test covering all four termination paths and the preview contract together.
fidelity_reason: Real server, PTY, signals and a scripted bridge; provider is the controlled dependency.
recommendation_reason: Broad cleanup matrix with repository-preservation evidence; keep.

behavior: Runs four invalid preview configurations (repository not allowed, unpublished source, wrong model, rejected credential) and asserts the validation-failed text, that no validated preview appears, the exact partial method sequence expected before refusal, and no CreateAgent/Send/CancelRun.
failure_caught: An invalid account policy, unpublished source, mismatched model or bad credential reaching preview or issuing a credentialed/catalog request.
criticality_reason: These gates prevent sending source context or acting under the wrong credentials; a bypass is a policy violation.
signal_reason: Each case asserts the exact method prefix (empty, GetVersion/Me, or GetVersion/Me/ListModels), so the refusal point is observable.
uniqueness_reason: Policy/model/credential refusal points are only covered here; the bridge-incompatibility row covers capability refusal.
fidelity_reason: Real CLI/server/PTY and a scripted bridge that records each method.
recommendation_reason: Four refusal points with exact protocol prefixes; keep.

behavior: Builds thirteen version responses (valid, three malformed capability types, a mixed list, six missing required capabilities, two unsupported versions) and asserts every one is refused with validation-failed text, no validated preview, and exactly one GetVersion method.
failure_caught: A bridge missing a required capability, carrying a malformed capability list, or advertising an unsupported bridge/protocol version being accepted into a credentialed or agent call.
criticality_reason: Bridge capability negotiation is the compatibility boundary; accepting an incompatible bridge leads to failed or unsafe remote operations.
signal_reason: The exact single-method event sequence proves refusal before credentialed/catalog requests across thirteen independent mutants.
fidelity_reason: Real server/PTY with a scripted bridge returning the mutated version response.
recommendation_reason: Dense malformed-negotiation matrix with a protocol-position assertion; keep.

behavior: Serves a version response with every required capability plus `future.unrecognized` and asserts the preview is validated and says terminal responses use exact-run verification, with no mutations.
failure_caught: A forward-compatible bridge being refused because it advertises an unknown capability (breaking future bridges) or the preview omitting the exact-run verification claim.
criticality_reason: Forward compatibility only; a false refusal blocks a newer bridge but has an obvious workaround.
signal_reason: The validated preview text and the exact-run line are asserted, plus a no-mutation scan.
uniqueness_reason: Only unknown-capability acceptance test; its sibling covers refusal.
fidelity_reason: Real server/PTY with a scripted bridge response.
recommendation_reason: Small distinct acceptance counterpart to the refusal matrix; keep.

behavior: Marks the fixture credential as missing and asserts the session shows `selected Keychain credential missing`, never a validated preview, and that the bridge event log is empty.
failure_caught: A missing keychain credential still starting the bridge or reaching a preview, which would attempt a credentialed call with no secret.
criticality_reason: Starting the bridge without the selected credential risks reading or sending with the wrong identity.
signal_reason: Two text negatives plus an empty event log prove no bridge start.
uniqueness_reason: Only missing-credential case; the policy/bad-credential row covers a rejected credential after start.
recommendation_reason: Exact no-start proof for a credential precondition; keep.

behavior: Sets TMPDIR to a regular file so channel creation fails, launches the CLI under /usr/bin/env, and asserts the session shows `invocation channel admission unavailable` with an empty bridge event log.
failure_caught: A failure to create the private invocation channel still launching the adapter or bridge, which would run without the supervision channel.
criticality_reason: The invocation channel is the authority boundary for the adapter; starting without it loses supervision and cleanup ownership.
signal_reason: The admission message plus an empty event log prove neither adapter nor bridge started.
uniqueness_reason: Only channel-creation-failure case; the CLI gate row covers missing admission earlier.
fidelity_reason: Real PTY, poisoned TMPDIR and a scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: No-start proof for the channel precondition; keep.

behavior: Installs a preflight helper that spawns a grandchild, waits for its pid file, then either SIGKILLs the adapter or lets the preflight timeout; asserts the scratch root is gone and helper, grandchild and adapter pids are all dead, with no bridge calls.
failure_caught: A preflight helper or its descendant escaping as an orphan after adapter death or timeout, holding the scratch tree and consuming process slots.
criticality_reason: Orphaned descendants are exactly the leak class the owned process group is meant to prevent; they can keep private workspace data alive.
signal_reason: Both termination causes are exercised, and three pids plus the scratch directory are each checked dead/gone.
fidelity_reason: Real processes and descendants under a scripted helper.
recommendation_reason: Multi-process descendant cleanup with two causes; keep.

behavior: Sends `prepare` and asserts the retained-handle text, exactly one CreateAgent and zero Send calls, and that the recovery field names handle restoration unavailable.
failure_caught: `prepare` sending a prompt as well as creating (an unintended remote turn) or not retaining the exact handle for later sends.
criticality_reason: Prepare must create exactly one remote agent and no message; an extra Send starts work the user did not ask for.
signal_reason: The exact per-method counts and the recovery reason pin both effects and the retained handle.
uniqueness_reason: Only prepare-without-send test; later rows build on it.
recommendation_reason: Exact RPC budget for prepare; keep.

behavior: For four crash boundaries (before dispatch, after create, after reply, after ack), asserts the offline retained recovery text, no auto-recovery, the exact CreateAgent/Send counts, the surviving creation-payload count, restart persistence of the same description, and that Discard/Delete are refused while the session is live/archived in the wrong order before succeeding.
failure_caught: A crash losing the original operation (so the remote effect becomes unreplayable/uncertain), auto-recovering without a claim, or discarding payloads before the durable state permits it.
criticality_reason: Crash boundaries around a remote create are the durability core: losing the intent orphans a possibly-created agent, and premature discard destroys the only evidence.
signal_reason: Four boundaries with per-boundary payload and RPC counts, an offline read, a restart re-read, and an ordering matrix for Discard/Delete.
uniqueness_reason: Only crash-boundary matrix with restart and discard ordering.
fidelity_reason: Real server, SQLite and scripted bridge; restart is real.
recommendation_reason: Durable-uncertainty contract with restart evidence; keep.

behavior: Pauses creation before dispatch or after claim, requests Discard, releases the paused adapter, and asserts the terminal text (admission unavailable vs retained handle), the recovery text `discarded locally`, no auto-recovery, the RPC counts, and zero payloads.
failure_caught: Discard racing a dispatch so a remote CreateAgent still happens after the user discarded, or the late receipt being adopted instead of reported as discarded.
criticality_reason: Discard is the user's cancellation of a pending remote creation; a race that still creates an agent leaves an unowned remote resource.
signal_reason: Both boundaries are exercised with exact creation counts and payload removal, and the post-release text distinguishes the two outcomes.
fidelity_reason: Real server/SQLite and a paused bridge at two boundaries.
recommendation_reason: Race resolution with RPC-count evidence; keep.

behavior: Installs SQLite triggers or corrupts/redirects the creation payload for six storage-fault modes, then asserts the exact CreateAgent count permitted by the claimed state, no Send, no credential or bearer text in stored metadata, and the receipt/closed fields reflecting the failure.
failure_caught: Dispatching a remote CreateAgent without a durable claim, or storing a secret in metadata while reporting a storage failure.
criticality_reason: The claim-before-dispatch rule is what makes a remote effect recoverable after a storage fault; violating it can create an untracked remote agent.
signal_reason: Six fault modes with per-mode RPC counts and raw metadata scans for a secret and the specific null/false markers.
fidelity_reason: Real SQLite triggers, payload corruption and a scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: Claim-vs-effect matrix with secret scans; keep.

behavior: Crashes creation at before-dispatch or after-ack, restarts, and asserts restart removed only the owned hardlink alias, kept the retired payload when appropriate, and issued no CreateAgent/Send for the retired boundary.
failure_caught: Restart deleting a payload whose remote effect is uncertain, or leaving an owned alias that later resolves to stale content.
criticality_reason: Payload retention decides whether an uncertain remote create can be investigated or discarded; deleting it loses the only evidence.
signal_reason: A hardlink alias and the canonical payload are distinguished by directory-entry counts, and the RPC counts are asserted per boundary.
fidelity_reason: Real restart, real hardlinks and SQLite record inspection.
recommendation_reason: Distinguishes owned alias from canonical payload across restart; keep.

behavior: Prepares, sends one inspection prompt, waits for `Ready: exact run fixture-run-1`, sends a follow-up and waits for `fixture-run-2`; asserts one CreateAgent, two Send/GetAgent/GetRun and zero ResumeAgent/ListRuns/CancelRun.
failure_caught: A follow-up starting a new agent or replaying the first run instead of sending to the same conversation, or a run receipt invented from an unverified observation.
criticality_reason: Exact-run attribution is the contract for cloud turns; a follow-up on the wrong agent or a fabricated receipt misreports work.
signal_reason: Exact method counts for both turns plus the two distinct run IDs in terminal text.
fidelity_reason: Real server/PTY and scripted bridge run responses.
recommendation_reason: Per-method budget across two turns; keep.

behavior: Configures an empty keepalive during send; asserts exactly one Ready line, one GetRun, saved progress send revision/token 6, and one unread receipt bound to CursorCloud with turn fixture-run-1.
failure_caught: An empty keepalive creating a second run receipt or advancing the send token, and a missing/incorrect unread receipt for the real completion.
criticality_reason: A keepalive mistaken for evidence would mint a phantom run and unread notification.
signal_reason: The terminal count, GetRun count, persisted token/revision and unread receipt identity are all asserted.
uniqueness_reason: Send keepalive branch; the observe keepalive row covers the cursor side.
recommendation_reason: Receipt cannot be minted by a keepalive; keep.

behavior: Drops the send stream after one event and the observe stream after four, with an empty keepalive in observe; asserts two observe requests with after values 0 then 4, saved observe revision/token 6, and one Ready line, where the exact after sequence [0,4] is the decisive assertion.
failure_caught: An empty keepalive advancing the observe cursor, which would skip a real event, or a retry that resets the cursor.
criticality_reason: The observe cursor is the only record of progress; advancing it on a keepalive loses events.
signal_reason: Persisted revision/token and the request `after` sequence prove the cursor did not move for the keepalive.
uniqueness_reason: Observe keepalive branch only; the send keepalive row covers the receipt side.
recommendation_reason: Cursor-position evidence across a keepalive; keep.

behavior: Uses opaque stream-scoped offsets and a replayed completion; asserts one Ready line, one `Inspecting selected source.` line, observe requests with after [null, "0"], saved send token "0" revision 2 and observe token "observe/result" revision 6.
failure_caught: The observer assuming offsets are consecutive integers (dropping opaque tokens) or deduplicating equal content so a real event is lost.
criticality_reason: Opaque tokens are the bridge's only cursor representation; integer assumptions break observation and can lose the completion.
signal_reason: The exact opaque token strings, after values and revisions are persisted-state assertions, not text matches.
uniqueness_reason: Only opaque-token test with a replayed completion.
recommendation_reason: Nonconsecutive-token handling with persisted cursors; keep.

behavior: Serves informational/future events around the completion; asserts one Ready and one inspecting line, saved send token 14 revision 9, and one unread receipt bound to the exact run.
failure_caught: SDK metadata or a future informational event being treated as the terminal result (premature Ready) or replacing the real token.
criticality_reason: Premature terminal classification marks a run finished and alerts the user while work continues.
signal_reason: Persisted token/revision plus single Ready/inspecting occurrences show the terminal event was chosen exactly once.
uniqueness_reason: Informational-event handling with the send token; the next row covers metadata before a disconnect.
recommendation_reason: Exact terminal-event selection with counters; keep.

behavior: Drops the send stream after metadata-only events and asserts the unknown/unverified text, no Ready line, null run_id and progress in storage, no unread, and zero GetAgent/ObserveRun.
failure_caught: Metadata before a disconnect being promoted to a run receipt, which would create a phantom run and unread.
criticality_reason: A phantom receipt is durable wrong state that later recovery or cancel would target.
signal_reason: Null run_id/progress plus absent unread and zero follow-up RPCs prove nothing was minted.
recommendation_reason: Null-receipt invariant with follow-up RPC absence; keep.

behavior: Serves an informational event carrying a foreign run identity and asserts unknown/unverified text, no Ready, no unread, no input requests, non-ResponseReady activity, and exactly one Send.
failure_caught: A foreign run identity being adopted as this session's completion, producing Ready/unread for work that belongs elsewhere.
criticality_reason: Foreign identity adoption attributes another run's completion to this session and can route attention to it.
signal_reason: Text, unread, activity, input requests and Send count are asserted together.
recommendation_reason: Identity fail-closed with attention-state assertions; keep.

behavior: For branch-only, exact-PR and wrong-head-PR modes, runs a fake `gh` that answers commits/compare/pulls, and asserts the terminal text is verified branch / verified PR / result link unverified, with no invented PR.
failure_caught: A PR link being reported when the PR head is not the exact branch head, or a branch-only result claiming a PR exists.
criticality_reason: A fabricated PR link misdirects review to the wrong change; this is user-facing attribution.
signal_reason: Three modes with independent fake-gh answers and exact positive/negative text assertions.
fidelity_reason: Real server/PTY plus a `gh` fixture standing in for the GitHub API.
recommendation_reason: Exact-head link verification across three shapes; keep.

behavior: Pauses send, enters a second prompt while busy, asserts the retained-locally text and exactly one Send, then releases and uses `/resubmit` to assert a second Ready with two Sends total.
failure_caught: A busy prompt being queued and automatically replayed (a second unintended remote turn) or dropped without retention.
criticality_reason: Automatic replay would send a prompt the user was told was rejected; dropping it loses their input.
signal_reason: The Send count before and after release, the retention text and the explicit `/resubmit` transition are all asserted.
fidelity_reason: Real server/PTY and paused scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: No-replay invariant plus explicit resubmission; keep.

behavior: Runs nine uncertainty/malformed scenarios, asserts each ends unknown/unverified with no Ready, exactly one Send and one CreateAgent, no ListRuns/ResumeAgent, and that Discard removes all payloads.
failure_caught: Retrying an uncertain send, treating malformed evidence as success, or leaving private payloads after Discard.
criticality_reason: An uncertain remote send must never be retried automatically; a retry can duplicate a paid turn, and malformed evidence must not become Ready.
signal_reason: Nine scenarios with per-scenario RPC counts, negative Ready text and payload-removal assertion.
recommendation_reason: Broad no-retry evidence matrix; keep.

behavior: Installs per-mode SQLite triggers (intent, claim, receipt, terminal, corrupt, closure) and asserts the permitted Send count, unknown/unverified text, no private payload or credential in stored metadata, null run_id for the receipt fault, one payload retained, and Unknown activity with no unread for the terminal fault.
failure_caught: Dispatching Send without a durable claim, retiring a payload that has no receipt, or storing the private prompt/credential in cloud_creations metadata.
criticality_reason: The claim/receipt ordering is the durability boundary for a paid remote turn, and metadata is queryable durable state that must not hold private content.
signal_reason: Six fault modes with per-mode RPC counts, raw metadata scans and state assertions.
fidelity_reason: Real SQLite triggers, payload corruption and scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: Claim/receipt matrix with secret scans; keep.

behavior: For four crash boundaries crossed with discard/not, asserts the actual Send count, a null terminal marker, run_id presence matching the boundary, discard payload removal, and no Ready text.
failure_caught: A crash after claim but before reply losing uncertainty (or claiming a run_id it never received), or a discard leaving the payload.
criticality_reason: This is the exact-late-identity core for a paid turn; a wrong run_id claim makes later cancel or recovery target the wrong run.
signal_reason: Eight combinations with exact Send counts and a run_id presence matrix keyed by boundary plus discard.
uniqueness_reason: Only crash x discard boundary matrix for send.
recommendation_reason: Boundary-by-boundary identity evidence; keep.

behavior: Completes one run (Ready), sends a follow-up whose reply is dropped, and asserts the activity becomes Unknown and unread is cleared even though no new run ID arrived.
failure_caught: A claimed follow-up leaving the previous Ready/unread state, so the user is alerted about a completion that is now stale.
criticality_reason: A stale Ready/Unread after a new claimed turn misroutes attention to finished work.
signal_reason: The transition from ResponseReady to Unknown plus unread None and a Send count of two pins the claim semantics.
recommendation_reason: Attention-state transition evidence; keep.

behavior: Serves a shell-failure discriminator that also looks superficially successful; asserts unknown/unverified text (not Ready), non-ResponseReady activity and no unread.
failure_caught: A contradictory shell failure being verified as a successful source read and publishing Ready.
criticality_reason: False Ready after a failed shell turn tells the user work completed when the source was never verified.
signal_reason: The negative text, activity and unread assertions pin the discriminator over the flat success shape.
recommendation_reason: Discriminator-over-shape evidence; keep.

behavior: Runs three success shapes (structured, flat, duplicated frames); asserts exactly one inspecting line, one Ready line, ResponseReady activity and one Send.
failure_caught: A duplicate frame producing a second Ready or inspecting line, or a legitimate flat success shape being rejected.
criticality_reason: Duplicate terminal frames would double-report and re-alert; rejecting a valid shape breaks normal success.
signal_reason: Counts of terminal lines, activity equality and Send count are asserted for all three shapes.
uniqueness_reason: Distinct success-shape acceptance; the contradictory row covers rejection.
recommendation_reason: Counter-based dedup evidence; keep.

behavior: Prepares, cancels before any send, asserts the local-stopped text, zero Send/CancelRun events, and a recovery reason naming a retained cancellation intent; then detaches.
failure_caught: Cancel before dispatch issuing a remote CancelRun (no run exists) or dropping the local intent so a later resubmit could still send.
criticality_reason: A local cancel must not contact the remote and must persist intent; the private content is preserved for the user.
signal_reason: Two RPC zero-counts and the recovery text are asserted, though no payload-content assertion is made despite the test name.
recommendation_reason: Local-only cancel with zero-RPC evidence; keep.

behavior: For four cancel-ack/snapshot outcome pairs, enters a partial multibyte prompt, cancels, asserts the requested text, that the RPC acknowledgment alone does not show a terminal state, then after release asserts Finished/Error/Cancelled terminal text, preserved partial Unicode input, exactly one CancelRun with the exact run, and no dispatch after a terminal outcome.
failure_caught: RPC acknowledgment treated as terminal evidence, a cancel targeting the wrong run, losing unsent partial input, or a later prompt dispatching after the run ended.
criticality_reason: Cancel outcome and exact-run targeting decide whether the user's cancellation is real; an ack is not evidence and a post-terminal dispatch is an unintended turn.
signal_reason: Four outcome combinations plus the pre-release negative and a post-terminal dispatch refusal, with the exact run id in the cancel event.
recommendation_reason: Outcome matrix with a decisive ack-is-not-terminal assertion; keep.

behavior: For five phase/boundary pause points, requests Cancel while paused, releases, and asserts the terminal text, the retained cancellation intent when the boundary is before dispatch, and exact CreateAgent/Send/CancelRun counts.
failure_caught: A cancel race replaying a creation or send that the user cancelled, or cancelling a different run after the boundary.
criticality_reason: This is the boundary where an acknowledged cancel can still race a paid remote effect; exact counts decide whether the cancel was real.
signal_reason: Five pause points with per-method expected counts and a recovery-text assertion.
fidelity_reason: Real server/SQLite and paused scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: Race matrix with exact RPC counts; keep.

behavior: Creates a hardlink alias of the paused payload and asserts Discard succeeds only after the root directory is empty, then releases the paused send and observes the refusal text and zero Send/CancelRun.
failure_caught: Discard acknowledging success while an owned alias (or the canonical payload) remains, which would leave private content on disk.
criticality_reason: Discard is the user's removal request for private prompt bytes; acknowledging with a surviving alias is a durable privacy failure.
signal_reason: The directory-entry count of zero before the response and the zero RPC counts after release pin the ordering.
fidelity_reason: Real server, hardlinks and a paused bridge.
recommendation_reason: Ack-implies-removal invariant; keep.

behavior: Fails the cancel intent or claim commit with a SQLite trigger and asserts the specific not-acknowledged text, zero CancelRun, no requested text, and the retained-intent recovery flag only for the claim mode.
failure_caught: A failed cancel commit still issuing a remote CancelRun or telling the user the cancel was durably recorded.
criticality_reason: Claiming durable cancellation without the claim is a false safety statement about a paid remote run.
signal_reason: Per-mode text, zero CancelRun and the mode-dependent recovery flag are asserted after the trigger fires.
fidelity_reason: Real SQLite triggers, server/PTY and scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: False-success prevention with per-mode evidence; keep.

behavior: Drops the send reply, cancels, restarts, asserts the cancellation-intent recovery text, that restart removed the owned alias while keeping the canonical payload, then Discard empties the directory with unchanged CreateAgent/Send/CancelRun counts.
failure_caught: A restart losing the cancellation intent, deleting unresolved content, or Discard issuing remote calls.
criticality_reason: Cancellation intent must survive restart; deleting the canonical payload would destroy the only record of a possibly-created remote run.
signal_reason: Restart retention, alias removal, payload count and RPC counts are asserted across a real restart.
fidelity_reason: Real restart, hardlinks, SQLite and scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: Intent durability across restart with alias discrimination; keep.

behavior: Makes payload cleanup fail by loosening directory permissions, asserts Discard returns an error and both entries remain, then restarts with permissions restored and asserts the retired text, an empty directory and one Send.
failure_caught: Discard reporting success while two copies of private content remain, or a later restart failing to retire them.
criticality_reason: A false success leaves private prompt bytes on disk; the user believes they were removed.
signal_reason: The error response plus entry count two, then restart cleanup to zero, pin the failure and recovery.
fidelity_reason: Real permissions, hardlinks, restart and SQLite.
recommendation_reason: False-success prevention with restart recovery; keep.

behavior: Serves an unknown-shape stream while the prompt is known to be observing exact run fixture-run-1, then cancels; asserts the unknown text still names that run, the cancellation names the exact run, exactly one CancelRun and one Send.
failure_caught: A stream failure losing the known run id so cancel targets nothing or a different run.
criticality_reason: Cancel must target the exact remote run; losing the id means a paid run keeps going or the wrong run is cancelled.
signal_reason: The terminal text naming the run, the cancellation text and the CancelRun event payload all agree.
recommendation_reason: Exact-run targeting evidence; keep.

behavior: Completes a run, detaches, changes the local default model, reopens with recovery_runs saying Finished, and asserts `Reconciled exact run ...: Finished` without Ready, no unread/activity/input requests, then closes with a stderr warning about continuing remote work, archives, and asserts the final RPC counts.
failure_caught: A reopen replaying the turn or publishing Ready from historical reconciliation, forgetting the changed local model, or closing without warning that remote work continues.
criticality_reason: Reconciliation after a detach must be informational only; publishing Ready would falsely alert, and a silent close hides ongoing charges.
signal_reason: The reconcile text, the absence of Ready/unread, the warning on stderr, the archived flag and a method-count matrix are all asserted.
fidelity_reason: Real server/PTY, restart-free reopen and scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: Reconciliation semantics plus a user-warning contract; keep.

behavior: Prepares a first cloud session, then a second session for the same account tries to prepare and is refused with validation-failed text and a recovery reason naming the original session id.
failure_caught: Two live sessions sharing one cloud conversation, so sends/cancel could cross-route, or a refusal that does not name the owning session.
criticality_reason: Conversation uniqueness is the ownership guarantee for a cloud account; sharing it would cross-route paid work.
signal_reason: The second session's refusal and the reason containing the first session id are asserted, though there is no RPC-count assertion.
recommendation_reason: Ownership-by-id refusal evidence; keep.

behavior: For six recovery mismatch modes (changed profile, credential, source, identity, unknown status, missing run), reopens the session and asserts validation-failed text, no reconciliation, and exact CreateAgent/Send/CancelRun/ObserveRun/ResumeAgent counts of 1/1/0/0/0.
failure_caught: Recovering under a changed account, credential, source or unknown run status, which would act on the wrong identity or fabricate a terminal outcome.
criticality_reason: Fail-closed recovery is what prevents a stale session from issuing a paid call under the wrong identity or source.
signal_reason: Six modes each assert the refusal text and a full method-count vector.
fidelity_reason: Real server/SQLite, git remote rewrite and scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: Broad fail-closed matrix with RPC budgets; keep.

behavior: Delegates to recovered_active_cancel("completion"): after a restart the run is reattached as unavailable with a saved cancellation intent, no CancelRun/ObserveRun is issued, `/retry-cancel` then reconciles the exact run as Finished with exactly one CancelRun and no Ready.
failure_caught: An active reattachment silently retrying the cancel over the old snapshot, or the completion path targeting a different run.
criticality_reason: The retry-cancel path must use the saved intent and an independent snapshot; a wrong target cancels or observes the wrong run.
signal_reason: The completion-only branch asserts the unavailable/retained text, zero pre-retry RPCs, then one CancelRun and no Ready.
uniqueness_reason: It is one mode of the shared recovered_active_cancel helper; the discard and storage modes are separate rows.
fidelity_reason: Real restart, server/PTY and scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: Retains the completion-mode evidence for the shared helper; keep.

behavior: Delegates to recovered_active_cancel("discard"): after reopen, runs `terminal cloud-discard`, then `/retry-cancel`, and asserts the validation-failed text with zero CancelRun and one Send.
failure_caught: A discarded recovered creation still allowing a cancel retry to contact the remote or claim success.
criticality_reason: Once the local creation is discarded, a retry must not resurrect a paid remote action.
signal_reason: The CLI discard success, the refusal text and the zero CancelRun count are asserted; the shared helper supplies the rest.
uniqueness_reason: It is the discard mode of the same helper, adding one CLI action.
fidelity_reason: Real server/PTY, CLI discard and scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: Discard-wins precedence with zero-RPC evidence; keep.

behavior: Delegates to recovered_active_cancel("storage"): installs a trigger failing the recovery-cancel claim, runs `/retry-cancel`, and asserts the validation-failed text with zero CancelRun and one Send.
failure_caught: A failed recovery-cancel claim still issuing CancelRun or reporting a durable cancellation.
criticality_reason: Claiming a cancellation the store did not record is a false statement about a paid run.
signal_reason: The refusal text and zero CancelRun/RPC count are asserted through the shared helper.
uniqueness_reason: It is the storage-fault mode of the same helper.
fidelity_reason: Real SQLite trigger, restart and scripted bridge.
recommendation_reason: False-success prevention in the recovery path; keep.

behavior: Drops the send after four events and observe after four with a replayed completion; asserts saved send token 103/revision 4, observe token 6/revision 6 (the decisive progress assertions), no prompt or credential in stored metadata, one inspecting and one Ready line, observe requests [0,4], and one Send/CreateAgent with no ResumeAgent.
failure_caught: A same-bridge observe retry repeating events (duplicate inspecting lines) or skipping progress, or storing private content.
criticality_reason: Transport loss is expected on a stream; a wrong cursor duplicates or drops user-visible events.
signal_reason: Persisted tokens, text counts, request after values and a secret scan cover the retry.
uniqueness_reason: Same-bridge observe in the successful-recovery direction; the next row covers rejection scenarios.
recommendation_reason: Exclusive progress across transport loss; keep.

behavior: For six adversarial observe scenarios (wrong run, changed or missing offsets, missing run, permanent disconnect, storage fault), asserts unknown/unverified text, no Ready, no unread or Ready activity, one Send, the allowed ObserveRun count (two only for permanent disconnect), and no ResumeAgent/ListRuns/CancelRun.
failure_caught: A foreign or regressed observe silently accepting a completion, or retrying beyond the allowed ObserveRun attempts.
criticality_reason: Observation retries are capped and identity-checked; accepting foreign progress would publish another run's result.
signal_reason: Six modes with per-mode ObserveRun counts and attention-state negatives.
recommendation_reason: Adversarial observe matrix with retry cap; keep.

behavior: Serves two equal-content events with distinct identities through a same-bridge observe retry and asserts both inspecting lines appear (count 2) and Ready appears once.
failure_caught: Content-based deduplication collapsing two distinct events, which would hide a real progress event.
criticality_reason: Deduplicating equal content hides progress; the consequence is a missing status line, not data loss.
signal_reason: The count of two identical text lines plus one Ready is decisive for the dedup rule.
uniqueness_reason: Only equal-content-after-interruption case; its sibling covers the send direction.
recommendation_reason: Distinct-identity evidence against content dedup; keep.

behavior: Serves two equal-content send events without offsets and asserts both inspecting lines (count 2) and one Ready with one Send.
failure_caught: A send stream collapsing equal-content events and losing one progress line.
criticality_reason: Same display consequence in the send direction, with the added risk that a lost event is mistaken for a stalled send.
signal_reason: The count of two identical lines plus one Ready and one Send pins identity over content.
uniqueness_reason: Send-direction counterpart; distinct from the interrupted observe row.
recommendation_reason: Small but distinct identity-over-content assertion; keep.

behavior: Adds a project with a workspace root that does not exist and asserts the directory is created, the registry stores the canonical path, and that a root under a regular-file parent fails with an error naming the blocked path.
failure_caught: Registration creating no root, storing an uncannonicalized path, or a creation failure not naming the requested path (leaving the user unable to find the blocker).
criticality_reason: Project registration creates durable directories and a registry row; the failure is recoverable by fixing the path.
signal_reason: Positive creation, canonical path and a negative blocked-parent error naming the path are asserted.
uniqueness_reason: Only AddProject root-creation test; other rows cover relative/invalid paths.
recommendation_reason: Creation plus error-identifies-path assertion; keep.

behavior: Sends AddProject with a relative workspace root and separately a relative repo, asserting InvalidRequest naming the rejected path, no directory created at the server's working directory, and no project registered.
failure_caught: A relative path resolving against the server cwd, creating directories or records at an unintended location and pointing the project at the wrong repository.
criticality_reason: Relative paths would silently place project state relative to the server's cwd, i.e. a wrong-target write and a misregistered repository.
signal_reason: Both halves are covered, with error text, filesystem nonexistence and registry absence asserted.
uniqueness_reason: Only relative-path refusal test for both fields.
recommendation_reason: Wrong-target prevention for both accepted fields; keep.

behavior: Checks out a feature branch in the repo, adds the project, and asserts checkout_name/default_branch, the protected root workspace branch equals the checkout, setup_pending is false, and the hierarchy root has that name plus a warning.
failure_caught: The protected root workspace recording the wrong branch (or default) so root warnings and subsequent branch bases are wrong.
criticality_reason: Root branch detection affects warnings and base selection but does not destroy state.
signal_reason: Five assertions cover detection, registry value and hierarchy projection.
fidelity_reason: Real git repository, server and registry.
recommendation_reason: Branch-detection projection evidence; keep.

behavior: Adds a project whose repo path is not a repository and asserts the error names the missing repo, the workspace root was not created, and its parents were not created either.
failure_caught: Validating the repository after creating the workspace root, leaving an orphan directory (and parent) for a project that was never registered.
criticality_reason: Orphan directories become confusing durable state and can later be adopted by a retry.
signal_reason: Both the root and its parent are asserted absent, along with the naming error.
recommendation_reason: No-orphan-on-failure invariant; keep.

behavior: Creates a worktree for a new branch and another for an existing branch, asserting branch/id/path, setup_pending false and a captured git identity matching worktree_identity.
failure_caught: A created worktree recording the wrong id/path, or no identity capture (later removal guards cannot verify ownership).
criticality_reason: Identity capture is what later removal guards use; a missing/wrong identity either blocks removal or allows removing the wrong tree.
signal_reason: Both creation modes assert path/id/branch/identity, and the test verifies the captured identity equals a fresh capture.
uniqueness_reason: Only new+existing creation test; naming/removal rows build on it.
recommendation_reason: Core creation contract with identity verification; keep.

behavior: Creates with base `--force` and with a tag as an existing branch, asserting the validation error text and that neither destination nor Git registration exists.
failure_caught: An option-shaped base being passed to git (argument injection) or a tag being treated as a local branch, creating a worktree at the wrong point.
criticality_reason: `--force` as a base is a command-injection-shaped input; accepting it can create or move refs unexpectedly.
signal_reason: Both cases assert error text plus absence of the directory and of a Git worktree entry.
recommendation_reason: Input-validation plus no-side-effect evidence; keep.

behavior: Creates with workspace name `../escape` and asserts an invalid-workspace-name error and that nothing was created outside the root.
failure_caught: A traversal name escaping the workspace root and creating a worktree at an arbitrary path.
criticality_reason: Path traversal writes outside the owned root, a destructive wrong-target action on the user's filesystem.
signal_reason: The error text and the absence of the escaped path are asserted directly.
uniqueness_reason: Only traversal-name test; the branch-dir row repeats traversal under a different dir mode.
recommendation_reason: Direct wrong-target prevention; keep.

behavior: Pre-creates the destination directory and asserts the create is refused with destination-already-exists, the foreign directory survives, and Git has no entry for it.
failure_caught: Adopting or deleting a pre-existing directory (another checkout) instead of refusing.
criticality_reason: Overwriting or adopting a foreign directory can destroy unrelated work.
signal_reason: The error, the directory's continued existence and the absence of a worktree entry are asserted.
recommendation_reason: Refusal plus preservation evidence; keep.

behavior: Creates with WorktreeDir::Branch for a mixed-case branch and an existing branch, asserting the slug path, the registry id still being the random id, no id-named folder, identity, and a traversal id still refused.
failure_caught: The branch slug losing case/underscore fidelity, the id being overwritten by the folder name, or traversal still accepted in this mode.
criticality_reason: Naming/identity drift affects display and later lookup but is recoverable by the registry id.
signal_reason: Slug, id, path, identity, absence of the id folder and a traversal negative are asserted.
recommendation_reason: Naming and identity invariant; keep.

behavior: Takes candidate folder names with a file, a directory, a slug collision, a deleted registered workspace, and a deleted-but-still-listed Git worktree; asserts suffixes proceed to -2/-3 and no foreign entry is reused.
failure_caught: Reusing a name held by a file, another record, or a stale Git registration, so the new registry entry points at someone else's path.
criticality_reason: A reused name makes the record address a foreign checkout, so later inspect/remove act on the wrong tree.
signal_reason: Five distinct occupancy sources are exercised with exact chosen paths and preservation of the foreign files.
uniqueness_reason: Only suffix-allocation matrix across occupancy sources.
fidelity_reason: Real filesystem, git worktrees and records.
recommendation_reason: Dense name-allocation evidence with foreign preservation; keep.

behavior: With WorktreeDir::Id, refuses exact and differently cased ids held by another project's record and by a deleted-but-listed Git worktree, while a branch slug still skips the differently cased folder.
failure_caught: Case-insensitive filesystem collision (APFS) letting a second record claim another workspace's folder, or Git failing after OVRCR already accepted the path.
criticality_reason: Case-insensitive collision would let two registry entries share one directory, breaking ownership.
signal_reason: Exact and cased ids, a Git-listed folder and a branch-slug escape hatch are all asserted with path errors.
uniqueness_reason: Only case-collision behavior for id dirs.
recommendation_reason: Case-insensitivity ownership evidence; keep.

behavior: For both WorktreeDir modes, asserts removal guards: unregistered, changes, clean removal preserving the branch, pruning a vanished directory, and refusing a foreign replacement even when forced.
failure_caught: A guard being skipped in one dir mode, so a forced removal deletes a foreign or dirty worktree, or a clean removal loses the branch.
criticality_reason: These are the destructive-action guards for both folder layouts; a mode-specific gap permits data loss.
signal_reason: The same guard sequence runs twice (branch and id modes), with branch refs and paths checked after each step.
recommendation_reason: Parity evidence for destructive guards; keep.

behavior: Creates a worktree, asserts inspect reports the canonical path, branch and dirty=false, then adds an untracked file and asserts dirty=true.
failure_caught: Inspection reporting a stale canonical path or missing dirtiness, so a dirty tree could later be removed without force or a clean one refused.
criticality_reason: Dirty detection is a guard input; misreporting leads to either refusal or accidental data loss.
signal_reason: Path equality, branch and both dirty states are asserted.
recommendation_reason: Small state-detection contract; keep.

behavior: Pushes WIP for a clean tree (expects no-unignored-changes), then for a tree with an ignored and an unignored file; asserts the branch ref and HEAD are unchanged, the WIP ref in the bare remote contains the unignored files and not the ignored one, and the worktree remains dirty.
failure_caught: WIP save moving the checkout branch or committing ignored files, or silently succeeding on an empty tree.
criticality_reason: Moving the user's branch during a WIP save rewrites history; including ignored files leaks build artefacts, and a false success loses work.
signal_reason: Both clean-refusal and real-save branches are asserted, with rev-parse equality, remote tree contents and ignored-file exclusion.
fidelity_reason: Real bare remote, git refs and worktrees.
recommendation_reason: History-preservation and content-selection evidence; keep.

behavior: Modifies a tracked file and asserts removal fails with worktree-has-changes, the directory persists and Git still lists it.
failure_caught: A non-forced removal deleting a worktree with uncommitted tracked changes (irreversible loss of edits).
criticality_reason: Deleting a dirty worktree destroys uncommitted user work with no recovery.
signal_reason: The error, directory existence and Git listing are asserted.
uniqueness_reason: Tracked vs untracked are separate rows; both are needed because the dirty check must cover both.
recommendation_reason: Direct data-loss guard; keep.

behavior: Adds an untracked file and asserts removal fails with worktree-has-changes and the directory persists.
failure_caught: A non-forced removal deleting untracked user files (the most common uncommitted work).
criticality_reason: Untracked files are unrecoverable after worktree removal.
signal_reason: The error and directory preservation are asserted.
uniqueness_reason: Untracked is a distinct dirty source from tracked changes.
recommendation_reason: Complementary data-loss guard; keep.

behavior: Registers a worktree created outside the project workspace root and asserts removal fails with outside-workspace-root while the tree persists and remains Git-listed.
failure_caught: Removal accepting a path outside the registered root and deleting an arbitrary worktree.
criticality_reason: A path outside the owned root is a wrong-target destructive action.
signal_reason: The error text, directory persistence and Git listing are asserted.
recommendation_reason: Root-boundary protection; keep.

behavior: Removes the registered worktree and replaces it with a different branch at the same path, then asserts both inspect and remove refuse with replacement/unrelated wording and the path persists.
failure_caught: A replacement worktree at a registered path being treated as owned, so inspect/remove act on unrelated work.
criticality_reason: Identity mismatch is the guard against deleting a foreign checkout that reused the path.
signal_reason: Both entry points (inspect and remove) are asserted, plus path preservation.
uniqueness_reason: Only replacement-identity test for an existing path.
fidelity_reason: Real git identity generation and worktrees.
recommendation_reason: Both readers of identity checked; keep.

behavior: Registers a path that differs from Git's actual worktree path and asserts removal fails with registry/Git-path-disagreement; then removes the empty registered directory and asserts the record can be dropped without touching the real worktree, whose survival proves no wrong-target deletion.
failure_caught: Removing by registry path while Git points elsewhere (deleting the wrong tree), or being unable to drop a stale record.
criticality_reason: Path disagreement is exactly the wrong-target hazard; a forced resolution could delete a different checkout.
signal_reason: Both the refusal and the safe drop-only path are asserted, with the real worktree's survival.
recommendation_reason: Wrong-target refusal plus safe cleanup; keep.

behavior: Removes a clean registered worktree and asserts its directory is gone, Git no longer lists it, and the branch ref still exists.
failure_caught: Removal deleting the branch as well as the worktree (losing committed history) or failing to remove.
criticality_reason: A worktree removal must not delete the branch; losing it discards committed history.
signal_reason: Directory absence, Git listing and a show-ref on the branch are asserted.
recommendation_reason: Branch-preservation invariant; keep.

behavior: Deletes a registered worktree's directory and asserts pruning removes the Git registration while preserving the branch; repeats for a directory already pruned outside OVRCR and asserts the stale record is removable with the branch intact.
failure_caught: A vanished directory leaving an unremovable record or, worse, pruning deleting the branch.
criticality_reason: Stale registrations block workspace cleanup; branch deletion would lose committed history.
signal_reason: Git listing and branch refs are asserted after both the OVRCR-deleted and externally-pruned variants.
recommendation_reason: Prune-plus-branch-preservation evidence; keep.

behavior: Holds the old admin directory open, replaces the worktree at the path, deletes the directory and asserts removal refuses with replacement/unrelated/identity wording and the replacement admin directory survives.
failure_caught: Pruning the old registration in a way that also deletes the replacement's admin data, corrupting an unrelated worktree.
criticality_reason: Deleting a replacement's admin directory destroys another worktree's Git metadata.
signal_reason: The error plus survival of the replacement admin directory are asserted.
fidelity_reason: Real git admin directories and an open file handle.
recommendation_reason: Cross-worktree metadata protection; keep.

behavior: Same replacement scenario without holding the old admin inode and asserts removal refuses and the replacement admin survives.
failure_caught: Pruning based only on the registry path deleting the replacement worktree's admin data.
criticality_reason: Same cross-worktree destruction risk, with less evidence available to the guard.
signal_reason: The error and surviving admin directory are asserted.
uniqueness_reason: Same guard without the held-inode signal; complements the previous row.
recommendation_reason: Proves the guard does not depend on the held inode; keep.

behavior: Deletes two worktrees where only one is registered, prunes the registered one and asserts the unrelated prunable admin directory and its Git registration still exist.
failure_caught: A prune sweeping every prunable admin entry, destroying unrelated workspace metadata.
criticality_reason: Global pruning is a wrong-target deletion of other worktrees' metadata.
signal_reason: Git listings for both paths plus the unrelated admin directory are asserted.
recommendation_reason: Scoped-cleanup evidence; keep.

behavior: Clears the record's git identity, deletes the directory, and asserts removal refuses with identity/replacement wording, the admin directory survives and Git still lists the worktree.
failure_caught: A record without identity being pruned anyway, deleting admin data it cannot prove ownership of.
criticality_reason: Without identity the guard cannot distinguish ownership, so pruning risks another worktree's metadata.
signal_reason: Error text, admin survival and Git listing are asserted.
recommendation_reason: Ownership-proof requirement; keep.

behavior: Attempts to remove a matching worktree that is absent from the project's records and asserts workspace-is-not-registered with the path and Git entry intact.
failure_caught: Removal acting on a worktree the project never registered (another project's tree).
criticality_reason: Unregistered removal is a wrong-target deletion across project boundaries.
signal_reason: The error plus directory and Git listing preservation are asserted.
recommendation_reason: Registration boundary enforcement; keep.

behavior: Renames worktree A and symlinks B's path into A's registered location, then asserts removal fails with unexpected-canonical-path and both worktrees plus both Git entries survive.
failure_caught: A symlink substitution making removal canonicalize to the other worktree and delete it.
criticality_reason: This is a direct symlink attack on a destructive path: the wrong worktree (B) would be deleted.
signal_reason: The canonical-path error and survival of both trees and both listings are asserted.
recommendation_reason: Wrong-target symlink defense with both-tree preservation; keep.

behavior: Switches a worktree's branch and then detaches HEAD, asserting inspect reports the new branch and a `detached @ ` label while the captured identity is unchanged, then removes it successfully.
failure_caught: Identity being tied to the branch name (so a switch or detach breaks ownership), or inspect reporting a stale branch.
criticality_reason: Branch drift is normal user behavior; identity must survive it, and a wrong identity would block or misdirect removal.
signal_reason: Identity equality across both transitions plus branch text and successful removal are asserted.
fidelity_reason: Real git worktree and HEAD state.
recommendation_reason: Identity persistence across normal git transitions; keep.

behavior: On a dirty, renamed-branch worktree: asserts non-forced removal refuses, forced removal succeeds, the repository-checkout root is still refused even when forced, and a forced removal of a replacement worktree is refused.
failure_caught: A forced removal bypassing the root or identity guard, deleting the repository checkout or a foreign replacement.
criticality_reason: `force` is the destructive escape hatch; if it also bypasses the root/identity guards it can delete the user's repository checkout or another tree.
signal_reason: Four guard assertions surround the successful forced removal, including a root-checkout refusal with the README intact.
fidelity_reason: Real repository checkout, worktrees and git.
recommendation_reason: Destructive-escape-hatch boundaries; keep.

behavior: Passes the repository checkout itself as a workspace to remove and to inspect, asserting both fail with repository-checkout and the README survives.
failure_caught: Treating the project repository checkout as a removable worktree, deleting the user's primary checkout.
criticality_reason: Removing the repository checkout destroys the project's working tree.
signal_reason: Both operations are asserted plus README existence.
uniqueness_reason: Only repository-checkout guard row (also exercised inside the forced test).
recommendation_reason: Primary-checkout protection; keep.

behavior: Asserts default_branch is main, then points origin/HEAD at a topic branch and asserts `topic`, deletes the local topic branch and asserts the resolver returns the raw `refs/remotes/origin/topic` string.
failure_caught: Default-branch resolution disagreeing with the TUI (so bases/warnings differ) or dereferencing a deleted local branch into a wrong name.
criticality_reason: Default branch feeds base selection and root warnings; a mismatch is a UX inconsistency with a workaround.
signal_reason: Three stages including the deleted-local-branch fallback are asserted exactly.
fidelity_reason: Real git refs and symbolic refs.
recommendation_reason: Exact three-stage resolver contract; keep.

behavior: Asserts no root warning on main; moves a feature worktree and the repo to new branches, runs observe_registry on a clone and asserts the clone's branches update while the original registry keeps its recorded branches; asserts the warning names both drift and default, then clears on return to main.
failure_caught: observe mutating the caller's registry (or failing to observe), or a root warning that omits the drifted branch or the default.
criticality_reason: Observation is a read that updates a copy; mutating the source would rewrite setup records, and a vague warning hides root drift.
signal_reason: Clone-vs-original comparison, warning content and the cleared state are asserted.
uniqueness_reason: Only observe-copy and root-warning content test.
fidelity_reason: Real git branches and registry structs.
recommendation_reason: Immutability of the source registry plus warning content; keep.

behavior: Registers a missing feature workspace and asserts observe_registry sets its branch to UNAVAILABLE_CHECKOUT.
failure_caught: A missing feature workspace keeping a stale branch name, so later operations believe it is available.
criticality_reason: A stale branch label misleads the Dashboard and later base/worktree decisions but does not itself destroy state.
signal_reason: The sentinel value is asserted exactly.
fidelity_reason: Direct registry observation with no git worktree present.
recommendation_reason: Small exact state marker; keep.
